title: Build a real fact-extraction Consolidator for the benchmark suite
summary: MockConsolidator (latency_cost suite) is a no-op cost-tracking demo, not real extraction logic — the retrieval-quality suite needs an actual Consolidator that turns raw WorkingMemory turns into SemanticFact records.
description:
This is the first of three sub-stories breaking up the largest fix this epic identifies: wiring the ENH-3 (Reconciler)/ENH-4 (async consolidation) machinery — already built and Done in EPIC-2 — into the benchmark's write path, which today (scripts/run_benchmarks.py) always constructs `MemoryStore` with `consolidator=None` for the retrieval-quality suite (the `--consolidator mock` flag only wires `MockConsolidator`, a cost-tracking demo used by the latency suite, into that suite — it does not run for `--suite retrieval` and has no real extraction logic even if it did).

Build a `Consolidator` implementation appropriate for the benchmark's synthetic, single-fact-per-turn sessions (an LLM-based one using the same local Ollama judge/model already configured, or a lighter template-matching one if that proves sufficient — justify the choice) that, given the raw turns `MemoryStore.remember()` passes it, produces `SemanticFact` records via `store.facts`. Wire it into `run_retrieval_quality()`'s `MemoryStore` construction (a new optional parameter, not a hardcoded default) so the retrieval-quality suite can be run with or without consolidation for a clean before/after comparison.

Before starting: read DECISIONS.md in full, including the ENH-3/ENH-4/PH-6 entries this depends on, and BENCH-1's findings. Before finishing: append a dated DECISIONS.md entry describing the Consolidator's extraction logic and its limitations on this synthetic dataset. Set BENCH-3a's status to "Done" in BOARD.html with a comment, then `git add -A && git commit -m "bench-3a: real fact-extraction consolidator for benchmark suite"`. Do not change the default `run_retrieval_quality()` behavior in this story — BENCH-3c wires it in and re-scores.

comments.text: Done. Built BenchmarkConsolidator in benchmarks/retrieval_quality/consolidator.py — a deterministic regex/template-matching Consolidator (not LLM-based; see DECISIONS.md BENCH-3a entry for full rationale). Classifies each WorkingMemory turn against four compiled patterns: dated events (confidence 0.95), explicit updates/corrections (0.95), direct attribute statements (0.90), project-naming references (0.90), catch-all (0.70). Returns one SemanticFact per non-empty turn with verbatim content and source metadata. Wired into run_retrieval_quality() as a new optional consolidator: Any | None = None kwarg — when supplied, constructs a local MemoryStore with the consolidator and enable_chunking=False (avoids the BENCH-1 ORC-2 chunk-path zero-recall bug). Default behaviour is unchanged (no consolidation). BenchmarkConsolidator re-exported from run.py for BENCH-3b/3c import convenience. All 542 unit tests pass; ruff clean. DECISIONS.md entry appended with design rationale, extraction logic description, and five documented limitations on this synthetic dataset.
